correctness.rationale: For every m>=2 and every continuous F in the specified toral homotopy class, the induced H^1 action of each delay coordinate is k A_m^j. The top-degree cup-product determinant is r f(m)Q(p,q), verified by explicit row reduction; choosing p=0,q=1 gives exactly the ideal f(m)Z. Injectivity of a closed-manifold self-map forces degree ±1, possible only at m=3. There the explicit integer delay matrix has determinant +1, and a C1-small perturbation has nonsingular derivative, degree +1 and is a one-sheeted covering. Smith lattice index proves optimal Fourier fiber count and exact cyclic generator; a separate unimodular two-sensor observation establishes the upper sensor bound. SymPy check executed from checks/check_delay_degree.py verifies all critical algebraic coefficients; no finite experiment stands in for universal proof.

value.rationale: The dimension-matched three-sample observation problem is intrinsic to delay reconstruction. The theorem gives an exact integer-degree ideal across an infinite natural family of exact nonexpanding systems, a robust topological no-go for every continuous nonlinear observable and dynamics in a whole homotopy class, and a sharp exceptional C1-stable positive reconstruction plus optimal cyclic Fourier aliasing and a two-sensor remedy. It is a motivated complete boundary classification rather than a single numerical computation; it makes no unsupported claim about more delays.
